title: Karpathy Builds 6,454-Video YouTube Rival in 2 Hours

body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Andrej Karpathy built HackerTube in two hours using Claude Opus 5.5, surfacing 6,454 videos from 40,000 Hacker News comments spanning 2007 to 2026.
- Claude handled the entire pipeline autonomously: downloading HN comments, filtering with Sonnet, extracting YouTube links, and building the platform.
- Karpathy's manual work was limited to creating API credentials, provisioning infrastructure, and registering the domain name.


Andrej Karpathy published HackerTube on October 31, 2026, a YouTube alternative seeded entirely with videos recommended inside Hacker News comments between 2007 and 2026. The platform surfaces 6,454 videos across 150 topics, and Karpathy says he built it in roughly two hours using[Claude Opus 5.5](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-claude-opus-5-5) as the primary driver.


## The Origin: Frustration With YouTube's Feed


Karpathy frames the project as a late-night reaction. "It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop," he writes in his launch post. His solution was to build a curated alternative sourced exclusively from Hacker News recommendations, a community known for signal-rich technical content.


The constraint was deliberate: no manual curation, no editorial layer, just whatever videos HN users have linked in comments over nearly two decades.


## The Pipeline: Claude Opus 5.5 in the Driver's Seat


Claude Opus 5.5 orchestrated the entire build. The pipeline started with downloading every Hacker News comment archive, then filtering to isolate comments that recommend YouTube videos. Claude Sonnet ran the filtering pass inside a Claude Code Workflow, narrowing the dataset to approximately 40,000 YouTube-recommending comments. From there, Claude extracted video IDs, queried YouTube's metadata API, and surfaced the final 6,454 videos.


Karpathy's hands-on work was limited to three tasks:


- Creating a Google Cloud API key for YouTube data access
- Provisioning a VPS to host the application
- Registering the HackerTube domain name


Everything else, including code generation, API integration, data processing, and deployment scripting, was delegated to Claude. "I don't actually do anything resembling traditional engineering anymore (read/write code, run commands in a terminal, or etc.), I only talk to Claude and have it do everything," Karpathy writes.


## Release Date and Availability


HackerTube officially launched on October 31, 2026. The project is publicly accessible, and Karpathy shared the build process in a detailed post the same day. The two-hour timeline includes the full stack: data ingestion, filtering, metadata enrichment, frontend construction, and deployment.


## Claude Code and the Workflow Feature


The build leaned heavily on Claude Code, Anthropic's coding-focused interface that has become the most-covered coding tool in AI news over the past 90 days. Claude Code's Workflow feature allowed Karpathy to chain Claude Sonnet filtering tasks inside the larger Opus-driven pipeline without manual intervention between stages.


This is not a one-off experiment. Karpathy is one of the field's most vocal practitioners, and his choice to publish this workflow as a normalized datapoint signals where autonomous development stands in late 2026. "This takes ~2 hours now," he writes, framing the timeline as unremarkable rather than exceptional.


## What This Means


Karpathy's HackerTube build is a public benchmark for Claude Opus 5.5's autonomous coding capabilities in production scenarios. The project demonstrates full-stack execution with minimal human oversight: data pipeline construction, API orchestration, and deployment scripting all handled conversationally. For teams evaluating AI-assisted development tools, this is a concrete reference point for what conversational delegation can replace in a 2026 workflow. The constraint that Karpathy imposed, limiting his role to credentials and infrastructure, isolates Claude's contribution cleanly and shows where the handoff threshold sits today.
